notes: Hindi (Devanagari) to Hinglish. Keys are NFC: a nukta letter (क़ ज़ फ़ ड़ …) is its consonant plus U+093C, taken before the bare consonant by the longest-key-first walk; ऩ ऱ ऴ stay single code points under NFC. Vowels are short (ा ी ू give a i u), which matches the most Dakshina romanisations; typed aa ee oo fold to the same skeleton. Anusvara and chandrabindu are always n; the pairs mb/mp/mbh/mph fold to nb/np so sambhav and sanbhav meet. Medial schwa: Hindi drops the inherent vowel in V C a C V (समझना samjhna, कमरा kamra, बचपन bachpan), which the walk keeps (samajhana); dropBetweenConsonants "a" drops every a with a consonant on both sides from the skeleton, so samajhana, samajhna and samjhna meet (smjna). On the Dakshina hi test lexicon (4,502 human pairs) the typed skeleton equals the walk's 76.5% of the time with it, 60.1% without. Not expressible in format 1: (2) The final schwa is kept after a conjunct ending in र य व (मित्र mitra, कार्य karya) and in one-letter words (न na); atWordEnd.inherent drops it everywhere (mitr, n). (3) े before a word-final anusvara is typed ei (में mein, करें karein); the skeleton folds ei to e, so lookup is unaffected, only the walk's spelling. (4) Anusvara is m before प फ ब भ म (handled by the mb/mp pairs).
